what_its_for: This medicine is an antibiotic used to fight serious bacterial infections in your body. It can treat infections in your lungs (pneumonia), skin, stomach, kidneys, and other areas. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It will NOT work for viral infections like colds or the flu.
how_to_take: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous line) directly into your vein by a nurse or healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT take this medicine by mouth. Each dose is slowly dripped into your vein over 30 minutes to 4 hours. Make sure to tell your nurse if you feel any burning, swelling, or pain at the IV site during your infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your kidneys are working. A typical adult dose is 3.375 grams to 4.5 grams given every 6 to 8 hours. Your treatment course usually lasts 7 to 14 days. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and complete the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a medical setting, doses are carefully scheduled and monitored. If you are receiving this at home through a home infusion service, contact your home health nurse or doctor right away if you miss or delay a dose. Do NOT try to double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: If you are receiving this medicine at home through a home infusion service, store the premixed IV bags in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze the bags. Once removed from the refrigerator, use within 12 hours if kept at room temperature. Keep all medicine out of the reach of children. Do NOT use if the solution looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles floating in it.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medicine. Avoid taking blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin) without close monitoring, as this antibiotic may increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid methotrexate if possible, as piperacillin and tazobactam can raise methotrexate levels in your blood to dangerous levels. Do NOT take probenecid unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as it can increase the levels of this antibiotic in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody, which could be a sign of a dangerous intestinal infection called C. difficile; unusual bruising or bleeding; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; muscle twitching, seizures, or confusion; signs of low potassium such as muscle weakness or cramps; or a new rash or blistering skin. Also tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Many patients start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important that you complete the FULL course of antibiotics even if you feel better sooner. Stopping early can allow bacteria to survive and come back stronger, making the infection harder to treat. Your doctor may run follow-up blood tests or cultures to make sure the infection is fully gone.
special_populations: Kidney disease: Your dose may need to be lowered if your kidneys are not working well. Your doctor will check your kidney function and adjust your dose accordingly. Older adults (65 and over): Elderly patients may have reduced kidney function and may need a lower dose or less frequent dosing. Pregnant women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Breastfeeding mothers: Small amounts of this medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose is based on weight and age and will be determined by your child's doctor.
